newsitem.title: USA: Consolidated Papers sees decline ending.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Papers sees decline ending.

text.p: Consolidated Papers Inc, which earlier reported a drop in first quarter earnings, said Tuesday the decline in business results that began in late 1995 may have bottomed out.
The company's first quarter earnings dropped to $0.63 a share from $1.18, primarily due to depressed selling prices for coated printing papers.
However, it added that measurable signs of improvement were seen during the second half of the quarter.
The company said demand for coated and supercalendered printing papers and coated specialty papers strengthened during the first quarter.
Operating rates at its paper mills improved over the same period in 1996. The company also successfully started up its newest paper machine, designed to produce coated specialty papers.
Total shipments for the first quarter stood at 430,122 tons, up from 368,038 tons in the year-ago quarter.
Shipments of groundwood-free coated papers were solid during the quarter, it said.
Consolidated Papers said its mill that produces groundwood-free coated papers improved to 100 percent of available capacity, compared with 86 percent in the 1996 period.
The operating rates at three mills that produce lightweight groundwood coated papers increased to a combined 91 percent of available capacity from 84 percent.
Its Lake Superior Paper Industries division, which makes supercalendered paper, operated at 96 percent of available capacity compared with 92 percent last year.

The Stevens Point Divison, which makes coated specialty paper, operated at 100 percent of capacity, up from 97 percent in the 1996 period, excluding a new machine. During the quarter, the company expensed about $2.0 million in start-up costs for the machine.
